newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels fear comrades will die in prison riots.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels fear comrades will die in prison riots.

text.p: Tupac Amaru rebels fear authorities will provoke prison riots to provide an excuse to kill the group's jailed comrades following the bloody end to Peru's hostage saga, a spokesman said on Wednesday.

"Their aim is to wipe out the problem and murder our political prisoners," Isaac Velazco, international spokesman for the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), told Reuters by telephone from Germany.

He said such staged riots were not likely to occur imediately, but it "would not surprise us" if they happened in the near future. Security forces have killed scores of jailed rebels while quelling prison riots during Peru's 17 years of guerrilla wars.

Velazco said he expected jailed comrades to immediately suffer physical and psychological torture after the failure of the MRTA's bid to force the government into freeing 450 rebels with its taking of the Japanese ambassador's home.

President Alberto Fujimori refused to give in to the rebels, who rolled back their demands in the last weeks of the 126-day siege that ended on Tuesday when commandos rescued all but one of the group's 72 hostages. The other hostage died during the rescue operation.
All 14 of the mainly teenage rebels died in the attack.
The MRTA had used the hostage crisis to call for improved conditions in what they claimed were "tomb" prisons, where torture of inmates was common.
